subjects.displayTitle: Contention and conflict: speaking truth without estrangement
subjects.introduction: Suppose you hold a conviction you believe could change another life. Bahá’u’lláh tells you how to offer it: in a language of utmost kindliness, and if it is refused, to leave the person to himself and pray for him, never to deal unkindly with him. A kindly tongue, he says, is the lodestone of hearts. The counsel reaches from the quarrel that begins as a joke to the religious controversy that ends in blood, and the Book forbids all of it. Two people may hold different understandings and both be acceptable to God; the moment they contend over them, both are rejected. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds the practical habits: resolve the slightest ill-feeling before it spreads, refuse to hunt for faults, meet a hostile thought with a stronger peaceful one, and when someone wants a fight, let it pass in silence. The Dhammapada’s observation that hostility has never been stilled by hostility raises the same question from another tradition: what interrupts the cycle in which injury invites injury? The answer is more than the absence of conflict, and the path continues into love and unity.
subjects.arc: Begin with kind speech, freedom to decline, and respect for rights; distinguish differing understandings from antagonistic contention; examine the damage of escalating conflict; then explore restraint, reconciliation, and practical habits of peace.

order.why: Place respect for every person’s rights beside the prohibition of contention.
shortened: Say: Contend not with anyone, nor deny any soul's rights.

order.why: Open with sharing a valued truth kindly and respecting refusal.
shortened: Consort with all men, O people of Baha, in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship. If ye be aware of a certain truth, if ye possess a jewel, of which others are deprived, share it with them in a language of utmost kindliness and goodwill. If it be accepted, if it fulfill its purpose, your object is attained. If anyone should refuse it, leave him unto himself, and beseech God to guide him. Beware lest ye deal unkindly with him. A kindly tongue is the lodestone of the hearts of men.

order.why: Read the Bab’s counsel to present proofs with courtesy and avoid causing hurt.
Distinguish acceptable understandings from the contention that makes them harmful.
shortened: For instance, one soul beholds the Unknowable and Inaccessible Mystery manifest in the Temple of Revelation without separation or connection, while another regards the Temple of Revelation as the Manifestation of God and His commandments and prohibitions as the very commandments of Truth. Both these stations are acceptable before the Divine Throne. However, should the holders of these two stations dispute and contend regarding these two ranks, both shall be and are rejected.

Nothing whatever can, in this Day, inflict a greater harm upon this Cause than dissension and strife, contention, estrangement and apathy, among the loved ones of God. Flee them, through the power of God and His sovereign aid, and strive ye to knit together the hearts of men, in His Name, the Unifier, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Consider practical intervention, counsel, and withdrawal when reconciliation proves impossible.
shortened: As for what thou hadst written about the fighting and quarreling of those associated with the Faith and others - you should stand aside and give counsel, using any means possible to stop the conflict and end the dispute. And if this proves impossible, withdraw. This is the way of the people of Baha.

order.why: Read the instruction to address ill-feeling before it spreads.
Join affection with refusal to hunt for faults.
shortened: Associate amongst yourselves with love and affection, and be not of those who search into people's deeds to find fault with them.

order.why: Examine idle dispute and the desire for superiority.
Read the body image beside the prohibition of striking and saddening others.
shortened: Beware lest the desires of the flesh and of a corrupt inclination provoke divisions among you. Be ye as the fingers of one hand, the members of one body. Thus counselleth you the Pen of Revelation, if ye be of them that believe.
Ye have been forbidden in the Book of God to engage in contention and conflict, to strike another, or to commit similar acts whereby hearts and souls may be saddened.

order.why: Keep non-oppression, kindness, and freedom from religious fanaticism together.
shortened: It is not permissible to contend with anyone, nor is it acceptable in the sight of God to ill-treat or oppress any soul.
It behoveth him who expoundeth the Word of God to deliver it with the utmost good-will, kindness, and compassion.
Should a soul fail, however, to accept the truth, it is in no wise permissible to contend with him.
In matters of religion every form of fanaticism, hatred, dissension and strife is strictly forbidden.

order.why: Read convincing explanation joined with acceptance of a hearer’s choice.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear God, shed not blood, oppose no soul, and be of the doers of good. Beware lest ye spread corruption in the land after its reformation, and follow not the ways of the heedless.

Beware lest ye contend with anyone, nay, strive to make him aware of the truth with kindly manner and most convincing exhortation. If your hearer respond, he will have responded to his own behoof, and if not, turn ye away from him, and set your faces towards God’s sacred Court, the seat of resplendent holiness.

order.why: Consider leaving a refusing hearer to themselves and trusting God.
shortened: Do not quarrel with anybody, and shun every form of dispute. Utter the Word of God. If he accepteth it, the desired purpose is attained, and if he turneth away leave him to himself and trust to God.
Such is the attribute of those who are firm in the Covenant.

order.why: Read the rejection of undue insistence beside friendly association.
shortened: But in this wondrous Dispensation, the Blessed Beauty hath delivered the friends from this heavy burden. He abrogated contention and conflict, and even rejected undue insistence. He exhorted us instead to "consort with the followers of all religions in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship".

order.why: Distinguish kind explanation from harshness and compulsion.
Read clear proofs in assemblies beside the warning against confrontation.
Consider the reported relation of differing beliefs, institutions, and freedom of conscience.
shortened: Some people acclaim Christ as God; others regard Him as the Word of God; still others, as the Messenger of God. These differences have led to contention and strife.

But Baha'u'llah has shut the door to such differences. By His appointing the Expounder of the Holy Word, by setting up the Institution of the House of Justice, which is the legislative body elected by the people, and by enjoining non-interference in matters of belief and conscience, Baha'u'llah has barred the way that would lead to disruption in the Faith.

order.why: Read the warning that both contending parties may fail the purpose of religious discussion.
Keep the reported application even to disputes concerning Bahaullah.
Read the reported distinction between a correct position and a harmful controversy.
Consider the reported warning against insistence that one’s opinion is right.
shortened: Baha'u'llah says: 'If two persons argue over a subject, both are wrong', so that no disagreement should occur. No one should say, 'My opinion is right.' He says, 'Both are wrong', so that no differences should arise among the friends.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between quarrelling and love.
shortened: To settle the dispute they submitted the matter to the Holy Presence, and the Blessed Perfection answered, "When there is a quarrel, all are wrong; but when there is love, all are right." The Blessed Perfection said the only thing that is not beloved is discord and all that is beloved is love.

order.why: Keep the instruction not to make claims about Abdul-Baha’s station a cause of division.
Hear the personal sorrow caused by unkind argument.
shortened: However, regarding this servant, I am absolutely not pleased that there should be any unkind words between two souls and any argument and dispute. I swear by the Most Great Name, it is as if an arrow has struck my breast.

order.why: Read the reported reaction to even a trace of religious discord.
shortened: All the friends of God know, and have read and continue to read in all divine Tablets and Scriptures, that at the mere mention of an atom of discord, the Blessed Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones) would become so inflamed that His blessed countenance would change color. And surely each person present has heard a hundred times with their own ears from His pure lips that He would repeatedly say with utmost emotion: "If I were to see that the Cause of God becomes the source of discord between two souls, I would abandon the Cause of God."

order.why: Consider the challenge to someone whose criticism reproduces the dispute being criticized.
Read the contrast between commanded unity and actual strife.
shortened: We have enjoined upon them unity; rather have they risen up in strife. We have summoned them unto wisdom; rather have they shown forth the reverse.

order.why: Examine denunciation and backbiting as sources of hatred within a community.
Keep the question about reconciling existing discord in its addressed setting.
Read the warning that trivial controversy can displace the main purpose of a community.
shortened: O teacher in the divine school! Your numerous letters were received, and their contents caused astonishment - what has befallen the friends of God that they have created such discord over a trivial matter, have ceased from diffusing the divine fragrances and exalting the Word of God, and have occupied themselves with these futile and useless discussions?

Rather, one must become heedless of and detached from all such matters and affairs, discussions and stories, and flee from them to such an extent that one should not even sit in a gathering where such talk arises, for discord will increase, clamor and tumult will intensify, the main purpose will be lost, all spirit and joy will utterly vanish, the external enemies will rejoice, and the internal opponents will be pleased and gratified.

order.why: Hear the concise appeal not to spend life on fruitless discussion.
Consider the danger of turning minor matters into recurring divisions.
shortened: In affairs, strive as much as possible to prevent differences from arising, not that every minor matter becomes a cause of discord. If things proceed in this manner, the end result will be pure chaos. All the friends and handmaidens of the Merciful must focus their thoughts on achieving unity and realizing the oneness of humankind, not that every minor issue becomes a cause of differing views.

order.why: Keep the reported observation of discussions that divide people.
Read the particular warning about interpretations within its own stated setting.
Keep the reported polemic about claimed inner meanings attributed to its source.
Read the reported caravan analogy as a warning about apparently righteous divisive claims.
shortened: In every age, whenever certain souls wanted to raise the standard of opposition, they would make some righteous claim, pretending their purpose was truth. They would use this as a means to gradually gain influence, then little by little promote their own aims. A skilled thief first becomes a friend of the caravan, showing great benevolence and kindness, until he leads the caravan near the thieves waiting in the mountains. Then it becomes clear he was in league with the thieves, but by then it is too late - the caravan has been robbed.

order.why: Consider the images of a fruitless tree and cold garden.
shortened: O friends of God! Beware, beware of discord, for through discord the divine foundation is destroyed, and through the winds of disagreement the blessed tree remains fruitless. The garden of unity withers from the cold winter of conflicting thoughts, and the fire of the love of God grows cold.

order.why: Read the extended warning about the consequences of dissension.
Examine the source’s concern for dispersed souls and lost confidence.
shortened: No harm has been or is greater to the Cause of God than discord, for if numerous souls act without wisdom and openly and manifestly speak the Word of God among people, undoubtedly this matter will cause agitation and clamor among the people.

Through discord, harm befalls the very root of the Tree, and beyond this, opposition to God's Command occurs, along with the dispersion of united souls, the waste of the Cause among the servants, and the bewilderment of weak souls - all of these things come to pass.

order.why: Read estrangement as a cause of declining energy and love.
shortened: But if discord and estrangement remain among friends, day by day the flame of the love of God will be extinguished and lethargy and stagnation will encompass all.
Therefore strive as much as you can for harmony so that 'Abdu'l-Baha may be pleased and spirit and fragrance may appear.

order.why: Consider the image of a small crack widening over time.
shortened: I swear by the Ancient Beauty and the Most Great Name that today even a tiny needle-sized crack will later become as wide as the distance between East and West, and a straw's worth of difference will become like Mount Qaf. All these labors will be wasted, the cycle will be destroyed and eliminated, the foundation will be utterly demolished, and the contingent world will be completely deprived of the light of guidance.

order.why: Read discord as fire threatening a shared harvest.
shortened: If they do not attain this unity and harmony, they shall eventually meet with manifest loss; confirmations and strength shall cease.
This is the fact and truth of this condition.
They must not complain about GOD. For discord is like unto fire cast amid the harvest. Therefore, expecting harvest under such condition is a foolish desire.
Thus the harvest should be saved and protected from fire that our hope may be realized.

order.why: Keep the pilgrim account’s poison analogy in its attributed form.
shortened: Disagreement is just like poison--whenever the poison enters the body it will kill it at once, notwithstanding its vitality and strength. So beware not to let this kind of poison enter your heart.

order.why: Read the companion pilgrim account’s clouds obscuring light.
shortened: Disagreement among the believers is likened unto the clouds which prevent the rays of the sun from reaching the space they cover although in a short time, the power of the rays will undoubtedly disperse the clouds, yet the clouds will stop the rays for awhile and temporarily deprive the creature of God from the privilege of enjoying the beauty of the Sun.
Disagreement among the believers has the same effect and result. It prevents the confirmation of God for a while. There will be no confirmation for any one as long as disagreement is in existence.

order.why: Keep the brief reported warning concerning lost spiritual receptivity.
shortened: Unity of the heart between the friends of God attracts the outpouring of the Holy Spirit and capable souls receive the bounty of the divine Mysteries and they become the distributors of the Light...
Inharmony destroys the magnet to attract the Divine Elixir and all become deprived.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between development through love and dispersal through discord.
Consider harmony rebuilding what lies in ruins.
shortened: O loved ones of God! Has dissention at any time borne fruit? No, by God, it ever strikes at the root of the tree of existence, while harmony transforms the ruins of the world into a cultivated place not of this world. The power of unity is transcendent over the power of the conqueror, and the unity of the hearts is the dispeller of afflictions.

order.why: Read the reported test of a religion through its effect on relationships.
Hear the reported invitation to gather on common fundamentals.
Consider the reported question about a short life consumed by envy and hatred.
shortened: The life of man is but a few days. Then death overtakes him. Is it not foolish to attach one's heart to its love and hate? Why should we let envy and hatred separate us? The strange part of it is that they have no outward existence.

order.why: Read the practical counsel to meet hostile thoughts with stronger peaceful ones.
Consider silence or inquiry as alternatives at the onset of argument.
shortened: Never allow anyone to argue with anyone else. As soon as discord arises, either maintain silence or ask questions. Argument, disputation and conflict between friends is forbidden - indeed it is more bitter than the venom of a serpent.

order.why: Read the instruction to show love and seek guidance during disagreement.
shortened: And if, God forbid, any difference, small or great, should arise between the friends regarding any matter, all must maintain complete silence, show love to one another, and inquire so that an answer may be provided. In any case, whoever becomes the cause of discord between the friends must be shunned and avoided.

order.why: Consider letting a would-be argument pass without reply.
shortened: Do not pursue arguments. If you see they want to dispute, avoid it and let it pass in silence.

order.why: Keep kind words as the permitted response to conflicting claims.
shortened: Whatsoever thou mayest hear of different and conflicting heresy, be thou silent and do not reply, except that which God inspireth thee of kindly words, which indicate the abundance of thy humbleness to God, and thy abhorrence of every talk that concerns worldly affairs.

order.why: Read restraint from both praise and blame in a particular situation.
shortened: They must praise those who are firm and extol those who are steadfast. They must leave every wavering soul to himself - no praise and no blame, no commendation and no reproach.

order.why: Consider the specific warning that joking can become serious ill-feeling.
Read the reported counsel to stop reviving old disputes.
Keep the reported advice about leaving divisive subjects unsaid.
shortened: Abdul Baha: Leave unsaid anything that would create disagreement. It is not necessary to touch upon such subjects. Baha'u'llah says that whoever is the cause of differences should be avoided. In any problem if two people disagree both are in the wrong. He did not say, one is right, the other wrong. This is said to prevent the arising of dissention.

order.why: Consider patience and forbearance alongside the prohibition of insult.
shortened: However, antagonizing or insulting anyone is not permitted. One must exercise patience and forbearance to the extent possible - perhaps God will bring about something after that.

order.why: Hear the brief rejection of harshness and severity.
Read composure and dignity in the face of opposition.
Consider the willingness to assist someone with whom there is no wish to quarrel.
Read steadfast, wise counsel intended to restore unity.
shortened: O My loved ones! Certain souls love those things that cause change and difference. Should anyone appear and utter a word from which the fragrance of discord can be detected, ye must counsel him with perfect steadfastness, with wisdom and utterance, that perchance he may turn to that which God desireth and be illumined with the light of unity and concord.

order.why: Hear the direct invitation to resolve existing differences.
Keep the brief wish for unkindness to settle.
shortened: Let no unkindness remain. May this dust settle.

order.why: Consider music and companionship as resources for ending estrangement.
shortened: I hope that in Shiraz thou wilt be engaged with melody and song, and wilt make the friends intimate companions and confidants of one another, so that this existing discord may disappear and this estrangement may end in unity, for discord and lack of harmony are the cause of bringing low the Cause of God.

order.why: Read the reported invitation to go home as friends.
shortened: Then to both he said, 'You are both right. But to contend will destroy you both. Go home and be friends.'

order.why: Hear the appeal to fellowship, wisdom, and truthful conduct.
shortened: Say:

"O friends! This is the time for fellowship and harmony. This is the day of oneness and of being everywhere united in speech. For disunity is tantamount to death and destruction, whilst harmony conferreth life and salvation. The glory of the Cause of God and of His loved ones dependeth upon unity and wisdom, whilst disunity, falsehood, and estrangement cannot but lead to the degradation and abasement of both.

order.why: Join reconciliation with friendship and humanitarian service.
Read the appeal to follow Christ’s example in removing enmity.
shortened: Therefore, all of you must strive with heart and soul in order that enmity may disappear entirely and that strife and hatred pass away absolutely from the midst of the human world. You must listen to the admonition of this Spirit of Truth. You must follow the example and footprints of Jesus Christ.

order.why: Consider the reported use of Quranic passages concerning distinct observances and freedom to decline.
shortened: God hath said in the Qur'an: "Unto every nation have we appointed certain rites which they observe. Therefore, let them not dispute with thee concerning this matter, but invite them unto thy Lord, for thou art assuredly on the right way." [Q22:67]; For every nation there is a path they follow, let them not contend with thee, summon them unto God, and if they accept, well and good, if not, leave them be. "I worship not that which ye worship, nor will ye worship that which I worship... Unto you your religion, and unto me my religion."

order.why: Hear the Bab’s wish that none should differ in religion.
Keep the Bab’s counsel about speech and protective withdrawal in its setting of possible oppression.
shortened: I counsel you, O concourse, that ye utter not a word that would stir up strife among the people, and that ye set apart from yourselves all who forge lies -- one and all. Verily, the Balance of Truth is in Thy hands: raise not a sedition in that land. And if any one of you know that the people desire to wrong him in aught, it is incumbent upon him either to emigrate by God's leave, or to hide himself from all men, one and all.

order.why: Read the companion advice about prudence amid danger.
shortened: Say: Thou knowest thyself better than I. If thou knowest the oppressors can affect thy Cause, then trust in God and speak not a word that would cause sedition thereby.

order.why: Consider collecting appropriate passages and sharing them with wisdom and joy.
Read counsel and attributes as the means of influence.
shortened: Dispute not with anyone, and remind the people with wisdom and counsel. O servant! Be adorned with My attributes, for We have lifted the decree of conflict and disputation and have manifested the Cause with power and might, without any from among the peoples of the world taking notice thereof, for power lieth in My will, not in warfare and disputation.

order.why: Consider character and deeds as the means of reaching hearts.
Keep wisdom and utterance within the image of winning hearts.
shortened: We have, in this Revelation, forbidden the servants from conflict and corruption and that which troubleth men of understanding, and We have commanded them to conquer the citadels of hearts with the hosts of wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read the stated dependence of triumph on wisdom and speech.
shortened: Conflict, contention and the like have been forbidden in God's Book, and the triumph of His Cause hath been made dependent upon and conditional on wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Consider the sign of the pen replacing the sign of the sword.
Read the source’s account of sheathed weapons through words and deeds.
Keep the account of transformed weapons as the source’s historical testimony.
shortened: For the protection and preservation of God's servants, this Wronged One, with no helper or assistant save a single pen, aided both government and people, and through loving counsels and wise admonitions removed killing and plunder from their midst. We transformed weapons into instruments of peace. For forty years no one has moved contrary to what God has willed.

order.why: Read the retrospective claim of forty years of prohibitions in its own terms.
Consider refusal of retaliation even amid a forceful account of persecution.
shortened: In this Most Great Revelation, the decree of the sword, corruption, conflict, disputation and the like have been strictly forbidden in the Book. If today someone should manifest evil intent toward the Wronged One, We would certainly not oppose him.

Although the hearts of the loved ones are wounded by the deeds of the oppressors - indeed the serpent and the wolf have committed that which hath caused the Messenger to lament in the most exalted Paradise, and the Holy Maiden in the highest Heaven, and the Supreme Pen in this most glorious station - nevertheless, obedience to God's command and submission to His ordinances are necessary and obligatory.

order.why: Read the rejection of killing within an address responding to events.
shortened: O Khalil! In all the Tablets of constancy wherein mention hath been made of grievous days, We have counseled all servants with compassionate exhortations that none should molest anyone, and no soul should contend with another. The decree of killing hath been entirely forbidden in the wondrous Tablets. Nevertheless, that which happened hath happened. Say: O servants of God! Defile not the good earth with the blood of idolatrous souls. The victory of truth hath been through goodly counsels and wise exhortations, not through conflict and contention.

order.why: Hear the complaint concerning bloodshed despite repeated prohibitions.
shortened: I complain unto thee of those who shed blood, after thou knowest that We have forbidden the people from this in all the Tablets - and God is Witness and Well-Informed.

order.why: Keep the explicit warning against the harmful action proposed in a letter.
shortened: After this was presented in the Most Holy Court, these exalted words descended from the heaven of will - His word, exalted be His glory:

Beware, beware lest thou commit what thou hast written at the end of thy letter. These are the deeds of the ignorant and the acts of the heedless. I swear by the Most Great Name that if any of the friends should harm anyone, it is as though he hath harmed God Himself. Conflict, contention, corruption, killing and the like have been strictly forbidden in the Book of God.

order.why: Read the reported preference for suffering harm over killing.
shortened: "Therefore the Blessed Beauty arose, with a divine power and might. He removed all of those implications, unfurled the banner of holiness, pitched the tent of universal peace and called the people to faithfulness, good morals and peace. He said, 'If you are killed in God's service, it is better than for you to kill.

order.why: Keep preservation of lives as the stated command.
Read the prohibition on killing a person of any faith.
shortened: O people of the earth! Associate not partners with God, and slay not anyone of whatever faith they may be, and dispute not with those who enjoin upon you what is good in the Scriptures and Tablets.

order.why: Gather prohibitions on bloodshed, unjust wealth, hypocrisy, and dispute.
shortened: And when thou beholdest the loved ones of God, say: "O people! Fear God, and spread not corruption in God's earth, and wage not war against men, and dispute not with them, and consume not their wealth unjustly, and refute not the truth by what ye possess, and say not that which ye do not practice, and commit not that which ye have been forbidden in the Book of God, and shed not blood, and engage not in that which displeaseth God's good-pleasure and your own minds.

order.why: Keep harm, treachery, slander, and denial of rights together.
shortened: Take heed that ye create not discord and dissention with one another, and that no soul harmeth another soul, and none acteth treacherously towards others, and no friend slandereth his friend, and no believer denieth the rights of his brother in faith.

order.why: Read unjust consumption of others’ substance beside bloodshed.
Keep the source’s historical account of prejudice and war attributed.
Read the reported struggle-for-survival analogies as part of its appeal to quench conflict.
Calls for harmonizing the world’s conflicting parties through love and unity.
Keep the reported comparison with animals distinct from its practical counsel about sharing a word.
shortened: Wild animals may perhaps by chance engage in strife and contention once a year, but human beings are perpetually in conflict and contention. For instance, a wolf may encounter another wolf once a year, likewise a leopard with another leopard, but humans are continually in strife and contention.
Censure stems from heedlessness of Truth; hence He says that if you possess a word of which others are unaware, share it. If it is accepted, well and good; if not, do not contend.

order.why: Read strife’s escalation into bloodshed and commotion.
Keep the Will and Testament’s prohibition and warning concerning aggression.
Read the Book of the Covenant’s categorical decree.
Consider the rejection of the sword as a means of spreading religion.
Read the contrast between removed discord and inscribed fellowship.
Keep advancement as the stated purpose of the prohibition.
Join humility and good qualities with refusal to wage war.
Hear the repeated prohibition in the Most Great Book.
shortened: Say: O friends! By the life of God, contention hath been forbidden, and conflict, corruption, bloodshed and evil deeds have all been strictly prohibited in My Most Great Book.

order.why: Keep the concise statement against conflict and corruption.
shortened: All conflict, contention and corruption are forbidden in this Most Great Revelation.

order.why: Read the judgment that discord is unworthy of the divine purpose.
Connect reform of the world with joyful association.
shortened: This Most Great Revelation hath appeared for the reformation of the world. Corruption and conflict are forbidden. The accepted souls must associate with all the peoples of the world with the utmost joy and fragrance.

order.why: Keep the brief categorical prohibition of disputation.
shortened: Disputation is never permitted.

order.why: Read the account of repeated prohibitions across the Tablets.
shortened: It is known to that being that from the Divine Source hath been revealed a binding decree whereby We have forbidden all peoples from strife and contention, from the shedding of blood, and from matters that are prohibited and that their minds abhor, to such an extent that it hath been explicitly revealed in most Tablets.

order.why: Hear the direct instruction not to make religion a cause of enmity.
Keep the compact prohibition of contention and war.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear God and contend not with anyone, nor wage war against any soul.

order.why: Read inflammatory conduct beside corruption and conflict.
shortened: Corruption, conflict and inflammatory matters are forbidden and unloved.

order.why: Hear the reported gratitude for release from strife and the command to love.
shortened: We have no quarrel with anyone, nor have ever had any.
Praise be to God, the Blessed Perfection made us free and blessed us with peace. He forbade us all conflict and strife and commanded us to show love and kindness to all in the world.

order.why: Read the affirmative call for loving association.
shortened: Corruption, conflict and disputation are forbidden. All must associate together with utmost love.

order.why: Keep the counsel to remove discord within its supplied wording.
Consider wisdom as the companion obligation to restraint.
Keep the short reported reference to the harms of argumentation.
Read the warning concerning dispute over divine matters.
shortened: As the Blessed Beauty has stated, if two of the divine friends engage in dispute and debate over a divine matter, it will lead to discord, and discord causes degradation of the Cause of God.

order.why: Keep the distinct reported statement about avoiding grief and sedition.
shortened: Be not the cause of grief, much less of strife and sedition."

order.why: Preserve the companion report separately with its own identity.
Read the contrast between forbidden and praiseworthy conduct.
Consider the removal of warfare and the injunction to what is praiseworthy.
shortened: We have obliterated from the Book strife and corruption, conflict and warfare and the like, and have enjoined upon all that which is praiseworthy.

order.why: Keep the concise prohibition in the Book.
shortened: Corruption, conflict, war and strife have been strictly forbidden in the Book.

order.why: Read the stated force of the prohibition in the Tablets.
shortened: He hath forbidden all servants in the Tablets from corruption, conflict and contention with a mighty forbiddance from His presence.

order.why: Hear the reminder of repeated counsel.
shortened: Say: O My loved ones! Time and again in the Scriptures and Tablets have We forbidden you from corruption and contention.

order.why: Keep the declaration removing contention.
shortened: We have removed the law of contention, for verily I am the One Who hath power over whatsoever He willeth.

order.why: Read the positive summons to gather together.
shortened: Say: O people! Gather ye together in the Cause of God and differ not concerning Him Who hath come unto you with every wise command.

order.why: Consider the warning about actions that cause tumult.
shortened: Any deed that causeth tumult and perturbation among heedless souls is not acceptable before the Wronged One.

order.why: Read the reference to multiple final Tablets as evidence for the teaching.
Keep the source’s affirmative statement of removed antagonism in its setting.
Read the reported application to quarrels over worldly matters.
shortened: Should two of the friends dispute regarding worldly matters, both shall fall from grace. Though they be unaware, divine bounties and heavenly confirmations shall be cut off.

order.why: Connect restraint with common origin and return.
shortened: In no wise is conflict and contention permissible. All have been created from one Word and unto that same Word do they return.

order.why: Read the warning that harmful conduct rebounds upon the Cause.
shortened: Strictly forbid all the divine loved ones today from corruption and conflict, for whatever occurs, its harm returns to the divine Lote Tree itself, as has occurred and returned in these days.

order.why: Keep fear of God beside the prohibition of conflict.
Read the denial that warring can represent a revelation of mercy.
shortened: Say: By God! The Ancient Beauty hath been sent with mercy and loving-kindness. Whoso associateth himself with Him yet warreth with anyone - God is quit of him and We are quit of him. Thus hath the matter been decreed in this Revelation.

order.why: Consider conduct profitable in both lives.
Read proof and exposition as the stated path to victory.
Keep the list of prohibited violent and corrupt acts.
shortened: Conflict, contention, corruption, murder and the like have been strictly forbidden in God's Book.

order.why: Hear the counsel to follow an example of noncontention.
shortened: However, thou must walk in the footsteps of the Wronged One and engage in dispute with no one regarding any matter.

order.why: Read the warning against transgressing the prohibition of bloodshed.
shortened: The shedding of blood hath been forbidden in the Tablet. Beware lest ye transgress that which hath been set down in the Book.

order.why: Consider wise remembrance as a response to religious difference.
Keep the acknowledged persistence of sorrow despite the teaching.
Read greeting and counsel directed toward shared conduct.
shortened: Convey to all the loved ones the greetings from the Wronged One, and forbid them all from corruption, contention, reprehensible deeds and unacceptable conduct, that the fragrance of sanctity may be diffused from all.

order.why: Hear the brief warning not to occupy oneself with disputation.
shortened: Beware lest ye occupy yourselves with disputation.

order.why: Read the prayer for protection from those choosing discord.
Keep the concise instruction against dispute.
shortened: Beware lest ye dispute with anyone, for this hath been forbidden unto you in preserved Tablets of might.

order.why: Consider disturbance of hearts within the source’s broader condemnation.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of the Cause that contention, corruption, conflict and whatsoever disturbeth hearts have ever been rejected and condemned by this Wronged One, as attested by what hath been sent down in the Tablets from the Pen of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read the brief rejection of mutual reviling.
shortened: Be not like those who revile one another.

order.why: Keep the direct prohibition of conflict and bloodshed.
shortened: Say: O friends! Conflict, contention and bloodshed are forbidden.

order.why: Read service as a response to estrangement and division.
shortened: Discord and division have been the cause and reason for the delay of the Manifestation of God. All must gird up the loins of service and remove estrangements and differences from among themselves.

order.why: Consider remembrance and utterance replacing contention.
shortened: God hath lifted the decree of disputation and contention, and hath ordained victory through remembrance and utterance.

order.why: Join the prohibition with the command to wisdom.
shortened: Conflict and contention have been forbidden in this Most Great Revelation. All are commanded to wisdom, and God Himself is powerful and mighty.

order.why: Read the counsel to avoid even signs of corruption.
Keep tyranny and enmity beside violence in the stated prohibition.
shortened: In this most manifest, wondrous and impregnable Revelation, We have forbidden all the servants of God from murder, corruption, tyranny and enmity, and all have been commanded to wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Consider purification of the heart as the responsibility of professing unity.
shortened: Those who speak and acknowledge the word of unity must purify and sanctify their hearts from corruption, conflict, rancor and hatred, that they may be adorned with the imprint of the seal "The Kingdom is God's."

order.why: Keep the concise judgment against corruption and contention.
shortened: By the command of God, exalted be His glory, corruption and contention are condemned in His sight. Unity and concord and love and fellowship are acceptable.

order.why: Read the stated intention to remove conflict from the world.
shortened: The intention and desire of this Wronged One has been to remove conflict and contention from the world. To this testify the atoms of all created things and the Tablets of God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Close the linked readings with kindliness as the affirmative command.
Keep the supplied counsel about worldly disputes with its own status.
Read the supplied guidance to explain a message without attacking other religions.
Consider shared work sustained by unity.
Close with the supplied provisional translation inviting mercy and growth amid differing understandings.
shortened: This one sayeth, "Thou art an extremist (ghali)," and the other one sayeth, "Thou art intolerant (qali)." This one adduceth evidence from a word of God, and that one reasoneth by another word of God. But I affirm unto them: Ye both are true and right, on the condition that thou not say unto him, "He is an extremist," and he not say unto thee, "Thou art intolerant."
Thus, wert thou to acquire wisdom, thou wouldst not reject anyone because of his limitation, but must foster the growth of all in the palm of thy mercy.

questions: How does the manner of sharing a conviction affect its meaning and reception?
What distinctions do the readings suggest between differing understandings, courteous inquiry, and harmful contention?
When might silence or withdrawal serve reconciliation, and when might wise intervention be needed?
How can efforts to end conflict also protect another person’s rights and freedom to decline?
How does the Dhammapada’s teaching about hostility invite reflection on the habits that sustain or interrupt a quarrel?
What practical change in speech, attention, or action might strengthen the love and unity explored in the connected subject?

references.note: Read the verses on brooding over injury, the inability of hostility to still hostility, and the effect of remembering life’s fragility. Compare them with the compilation’s counsels on kind speech, restraint, and reconciliation. How might changing one’s response interrupt a cycle of mutual harm?

subjects.displayTitle: Proclamation to the people of the Bayán: promise, recognition, and response
subjects.introduction: By what proof did you believe in the Primal Point? That is the question Bahá’u’lláh puts to the followers of the Báb, and it makes a community’s own history the standard for judging the claim now before it. The Báb had called the Bayán a gift for Him Whom God shall make manifest, and had warned that its letters might one day veil its readers from its purpose. So the address asks for fairness: come and hear the verses as they are revealed, look with your own eyes rather than through inherited names, and do not repeat the arguments once used against the Báb himself. Invitation stands beside lament and sharp rebuke, and the rebuke belongs to its contested hour rather than to anyone today. Beneath it lies the question Jesus pressed on those who searched the scriptures yet refused their witness: what fidelity to a text asks when the text points beyond itself. The journey continues into prayer for the Bábís, the pattern of prophecy and fulfilment, and the proclamation addressed to kings, clergy and the peoples of the world.
subjects.arc: Begin with fairness and consistent standards of recognition; read the Bab’s expectation and the claimed relationship to the Bayan; examine names, authority, and direct encounter; then follow the calls to mercy, steadfastness, and action.

order.why: Read the Bab’s warning against becoming veiled from the promised Manifestation.
shortened: O congregation of the Bayan, and all who are therein! Recognize ye the limits imposed upon you, for such a One as the Point of the Bayan Himself hath believed in Him Whom God shall make manifest, before all things were created. Therein, verily, do I glory before all who are in the kingdom of heaven and earth. Suffer not yourselves to be shut out as by a veil from God after He hath revealed Himself.

order.why: Open by asking readers to examine the proof on which their earlier belief rested.
Read the invitation to come and see alongside a demand for fairness.
Consider the call to speak justly after witnessing signs.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan, be fair and speak with justice. Be not of those who, after witnessing, denied, nor of those concerning whom the Desired One of all creation hath said in the Qur'an: "How many a sign do they pass by and turn away therefrom!"

order.why: Keep the Bab’s expectation and the image of fruits within the community’s own scripture.
shortened: O people of the Bayan! Ye shall surely ask from Him Whom God shall make manifest and aid in this matter according to your ability. God shall raise up from the Manifestation of His Self one of Truth from among those who are His chosen ones and who stand firm in His Cause.
O people of the Bayan! Ye are the fruits of your own selves. Waste not yourselves, but manifest all that ye perform in secret on the Day of Resurrection, if ye be sincere in your deeds.

order.why: Calls the people of the Bayan to recognize and assist the promised Manifestation.
Read the Bayan offered as a gift to its anticipated recipient.
Examine the warning that the text and its letters can obstruct their own purpose.
Bring recognition into a remembered relationship of care and daily companionship.
Consider the invitation to hear verses at their revelation.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan, present yourselves before the Divine Countenance that ye may hear the verses at the time of their revelation. Beware lest the ignorant ones among the people who have denied God's verses prevent you from this bounty, the Lord of lords.

order.why: Keep the companion challenge about consistent evidence as a distinct passage.
Read the question linking prior belief and present rejection.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By what proof did ye believe in the All-Merciful, and by what evidence did ye turn away from Him Who, when He appeared, caused the Spirit to proclaim before His face: "The Hidden One hath appeared with manifest sovereignty!"

order.why: Examine the demand to identify the proof sustaining a claim of faith.
Consider fair judgment of the revealed words.
Read fairness as a response to a claimed center of nearness.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, then judge with fairness concerning that which hath appeared at this Station which God hath made the point round which circle them who are nigh unto Him from all eternity.

order.why: Keep the concise instruction to judge fairly.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Judge fairly in this Cause and follow not every heedless doubter.

order.why: Join direct observation and equity with the claim of present revelation.
Read the question of where one will turn if the speaker is denied.
shortened: The Tongue of God speaks and bears witness to the Beauty of the Promised One Who has appeared with manifest sovereignty, and says: O people of the Bayan! Be fair in the name of your Lord, the All-Merciful. If you deny Him Who speaks the truth, to whom will you turn?

order.why: Consider evidence and the obligation to judge beyond others’ rejection.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Be fair in judging God's proof and His evidence, His glory and His grandeur and His sovereignty. Beware lest you follow those who have violated God's covenant and testament and denied what has been sent down from the heaven of His grace upon His servants.

order.why: Read the call to fairness amid signs filling the horizons.
Keep fairness beside the warning not to oppose.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and oppose not Him through Whom the decree of God hath been established, both in the past and in the future. Be fair-minded, and be not of the wrongdoers.

order.why: Read the warning against adopting the desires of others.
Consider the rebuke of idle dispute alongside the call to pure sight and truthful speech.
Read fear of God and the gift of understanding together.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! The head of wisdom is the fear of God. Fear ye Him Who created you and raised you to the heavens of knowledge, and sent down unto you wisdom and utterance, and made you to be among those endowed with understanding.

order.why: Consider the demand to learn from past error and use a precious present.
Keep the Bab’s direct address concerning the Mirror and the Bayan in its own textual setting.
shortened: Fear ye God, O people of the Bayan, then fear ye Me. Verily I am the Mirror of God, my Lord; all turn unto Me. Verily I commune from the most exalted horizon. I hear what ye utter and observe what ye do. No seeker shall petition Me through the Bayan but that I shall grant it for the sake of God, the All-Powerful, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Read the Bayan as a ring and leaf within the will of its promised figure.
Consider the specific reference to the Book of the Temples and the Judge.
Keep the cited revelation concerning the Hidden Name within the passage’s argument.
Read the claim that the Primal Point took the later covenant before His own.
Consider the companion statement about covenant in the atoms of the Bayan.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! The Chosen One took from you the covenant of My Self in the atoms of the Bayan before the mention of His own Self. Beware lest ye break God's covenant, for whoso breaketh it is indeed in manifest loss.

order.why: Read the instruction to behold with His own eyes rather than through letters and mirrors.
Keep the relation between beginning, culmination, and required recognition as stated.
Read the claim that the Bayan and Tablets were revealed for this remembrance.
Consider the concise claim concerning the entire Bayan’s purpose.
Return to the image of the Bayan as a gift.
shortened: Rise and say: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful. Do ye object to Him Whom God hath made the Dawning-Place of His power and sovereignty, and made the Bayan a gift unto His Own Self? Fear God and follow not every doubting idolator.

order.why: Keep the stated honor of the Bayan through the promised figure within its forceful address.
shortened: Arise in My Name and say: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful and follow not every accursed Satan. By God! He hath come through Whose praise and mention the Bayan was honored - to this do those who are fair-minded bear witness.

order.why: Read the brief declaration of a Book as proof to the people of the Bayan.
Examine the commentary’s claim concerning the Herald’s intended purpose.
Read the cited statement about the unknown time of revelation within its polemical frame.
Consider the question whether revelation depends on conditions set by its audience.
Keep the companion questions about stipulation and divine initiative.
Read the meaning assigned to freedom of divine action.
shortened: O Nasru'llah! Say: O deniers of the Bayan! "He doeth what He willeth" hath ever been and shall ever be the truth. No affair among affairs and no deed among deeds is hidden from Him. Were they to drink from the ocean of this blessed Word, they would be enabled by the blessed words "We turn unto Thee."

order.why: Consider looking at what the claimant presents rather than only what one already possesses.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful and speak not that which would cause the hearts of them who are nigh unto God to burn. He hath come as He willeth. The command is in God's hands - He ordaineth what He pleaseth. Verily He is the Almighty, the Powerful. Look ye at what He possesseth, not at what ye possess. This is what We counsel you in the Tablets. Read them and follow not the ways of the calumniators.
Say: If ye deny Him Who speaketh between earth and heaven, unto whom will ye turn? Consider, if ye be of the truthful.

order.why: Read the invitation to encounter beside the claim of self-sufficient proof.
shortened: Say: Be fair, O people of the Bayan, concerning this Book which God hath made the point round which circle all the books of the world, and this Remembrance before which all remembrances bow down. Say: Present yourselves before the Face that your eyes may behold what no eyes have seen and your ears may hear what no ears have heard. He is the One Who cannot be known except through Himself and Who needeth not the testimony of scriptures, books and tablets to prove His Cause.

order.why: Keep the concise claim that no outside proof is needed.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! He Who speaketh before all faces hath no need of aught else to prove His Cause.

order.why: Consider the warning about the limits of indications in books.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By God, the All-Merciful hath come, and He cannot be indicated by the indications in the books of earth, nor by what the Daysprings of existence have uttered.

order.why: Read the tension between not testing revelation and being invited to hear it.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! It behooveth no one to test the Dawning-Places of God's Revelation, the Mighty, the All-Praised. Yet the Wronged One summoneth you and biddeth you to present yourselves that ye may hear that which is sent down from the heaven of the Will of God, the Lord of the Day of Judgment.

order.why: Keep the bird-voice comparisons as the source’s argument for discernment.
Read the denial of seeking the audience’s existing claims or possessions.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By the life of God! I have not claimed that which ye possess, nor do I desire to establish for Myself that which ye have.

order.why: Consider the account of being awakened and made to speak beyond named offices.
Read the testimony that speech does not proceed from personal desire.
Examine the warning against attachment to names.
Keep the brief observation of continued attachment to familiar names.
Read the call to leave the idols of names and turn toward God.
Consider the injunction to pass beyond competing names.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Open your eyes! Today is not the day for mentioning names. Pass by that which is neither worthy nor befitting. Defile not the Day of God with mention of this one and that one.
Verily He hath appeared and come, despite those who follow self and passion.

order.why: Read the ocean of meanings as an alternative to fixation on names.
Keep the stated relation between the Bayan and the newly speaking Book.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan, cast aside what ye possess and take what ye have been given from the presence of an ancient Bestower. The Bayan profiteth you not except through this mighty and exalted Book.

order.why: Read certitude and the speaking Book beside the limits of existing books.
Consider release of what is possessed to turn toward the countenance.
shortened: O people of the Bayan! The All-Merciful hath come, and that which ye possess shall profit you not this day. Cast it aside in My Name, then turn ye toward the light of the Countenance, as commanded by God, the Ordainer, the Most Praiseworthy.

order.why: Read the warning against making outward religious symbols new veils.
Keep the brief appeal not to repeat earlier rejection.
Read the personal address leading into a call to leave imaginings.
Consider the hidden becoming visible and the turn toward light.
Keep the direct counsel to leave idle imaginings.
shortened: Fear ye God, O people of the Bayan, and follow not the manifestations of fancy and vain imaginings.

order.why: Read the alternative of attending to what is commanded.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear the Most Merciful and follow not your idle fancies. Follow that which ye have been commanded by One All-Knowing, All-Informed.

order.why: Consider proof and evidence beside the rejection of fancy.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and follow not your idle fancies. Follow Him through Whom the proof hath been established and the evidence made clear.

order.why: Read the appeal to follow inspiration rather than self.
Keep the companion summons concerning a command beyond earthly resistance.
Read the warning against assuming an unappointed claim.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful. Follow Him before Whom the verses have prostrated themselves and to Whom the necks of the proud have been humbled. Beware lest ye claim that which hath not been ordained for you by your Lord, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

order.why: Consider nearness of servants as the stated purpose of remembrance.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By the life of the All-Merciful! He desired no mention from among all mentions except for the drawing near of the servants and their turning to God, the Lord of the Day of Return.

order.why: Hear the Dove’s invitation through love, longing, and self-effacement.
shortened: O people of the Bayan and whosoever hath believed in God and His verses in the realm of exposition! Hearken unto that which the Dove of Identity warbleth unto you from the uttermost heights of Its ecstasy in the love of God and the pinnacle of Its passionate longing for God, Its self-effacement and Its subsistence in God, the All-Powerful, the All-Compelling.

order.why: Read the chosen audience’s opportunity and the danger of veils.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! We have chosen you out of the world to know and recognize Our Self. We have caused you to draw nigh unto the right side of Paradise—the Spot out of which the undying Fire crieth in manifold accents: “There is none other God besides Me, the All-Powerful, the Most High!” Take heed lest ye allow yourselves to be shut out as by a veil from this Daystar that shineth above the dayspring of the Will of your Lord, the All-Merciful, and whose light hath encompassed both the small and the great.

order.why: Keep the addressed proclamation through the images of dawn and life-giving wine.
Read the geometrical and burning-fire imagery in its own mystical terms.
Consider revelation in clouds accompanied by dominion and might.
Keep the severe rebuke alongside the passage’s images of disclosed treasure and Sinai.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Die in your wrath! The Hidden Treasure hath appeared, and He Who was concealed in God's knowledge, the Lord of all men, hath been made manifest. Say: The Sun hath risen, and the Light hath shone forth, and the Fire in the Tree on Sinai doth call aloud and give glad-tidings unto the people of this Revelation which was promised in the Books of God, the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Read opened gates of grace beside the warning against following oppressors.
Hear the proclamation of the one announced in earlier Books.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful. He of Whom mention was made in the Books of God hath come, and the Point of the Bayan gave glad-tidings of Him, would that ye might know!

order.why: Keep the concise declaration of the Expected One’s appearance.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By God, the Truth! The Expected One hath appeared and we have truly submitted ourselves unto Him.

order.why: Read the brief image of knowledge’s treasure made manifest.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! That which lay treasured in the divine repository of knowledge hath appeared.

order.why: Connect the Bayan’s central promise with the voice on Sinai.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! He around Whom the Bayan revolved hath come, and that which was mentioned by the tongue of the Point, Who gave the glad tidings to the servants of the appearance of Him Who conversed on Sinai, hath been made manifest in this mighty and wondrous station.

order.why: Read the call to judge a proclamation attributed to earlier prophetic witness.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Judge fairly concerning this Announcement which Muhammad, the Messenger of God, foretold, and unto whose mention the Point of the Bayan bowed down.

order.why: Consider the appeal to Muhammad, Moses, and Jesus in the source’s fulfillment claim.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, then judge with fairness concerning this Cause, whereof Muhammad the Apostle of God gave tidings, and the One Who conversed with God warned of, and the Spirit gave glad-tidings of.

order.why: Read the appeal to the Quran, Gospel, and Psalms with its claimed continuity.
Keep the Quranic allusion to standing before the Lord within the address.
Read the voice of the Primal Point and the cited Quranic promise.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful. This is the Primal Point, Who circles round the Throne and proclaims with His most exalted call: "O my people! This is He Whom I gave you glad tidings of in the Books of God and what the All-Merciful revealed in the Furqan through His words 'the Day when thy Lord cometh, or some of the signs of thy Lord,' if ye be of those who know.

order.why: Keep the particular claim concerning Husayn after the Qaim in its own terms.
shortened: O Husayn! Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful. This is that Husayn Who was promised in the Book of God, the Lord of lords. Verily, He hath appeared after the Qa'im with a Cause before which all who are in earth and heaven shall not stand. Cast away your vain imaginings.

order.why: Consider the paired banners of divine identity and freedom of action.
Read the raised pavilion and circulating water as proclamation imagery.
Keep the brief declaration that the matter has been decided.
Hear the compact proclamation of sovereignty.
Read the concise announcement of certitude.
Keep the stated appearance despite the audience’s wishes.
Read the speaker’s relation to divine will and the solitary stand before the world.
Consider the compact appeal to clear proof and moral response.
Read the warning against opposing perfected evidence.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the Most Merciful, and oppose not Him through Whom the proof hath been perfected and the evidence made manifest.

order.why: Keep the bewilderment concerning rejection of offered signs.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! The hearts of them that are nigh unto God are bewildered at you. I know not what ye desire, O ye heedless ones! If ye seek God's signs, by God they have descended in the most wondrous utterance, to which every thing beareth witness, if ye be of them that deny.

order.why: Consider the question about denying the source of familiar wisdom.
shortened: The Unseen from the horizon of appearance now speaketh and saith: "O people of the Bayan! Have ye denied the All-Merciful after that through which My wisdom was made manifest amongst the servants and through which the standards of the Cause were raised in all lands?"

order.why: Read the voiced identity with Ali and the warning against repeating a former response.
Consider the burning-tree voice and the danger of names as veils.
shortened: From the Burning Bush beyond the Radiant City upon the hallowed Spot of God's Command, the Mystery of God hath, by the power of the spirit, been witnessed, and speaketh in truth saying: "O people of the Bayan! Have ye disbelieved in the One through Whom ye believed in God aforetime? Here is My Beauty, which hath been revealed through His grace; yet have ye allowed them that are the manifestations of names in the kingdom of creation to shut you out therefrom; notwithstanding that they were all created by His Word.

order.why: Face the charge of using former verses to deny their speaker.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Do ye claim faith within yourselves and seek to prove your cause through My verses revealed aforetime, yet deny My Self? Alas for you, O company of unbelievers! By the True One! Ye have committed that which no peoples before you have committed, as doth bear witness the Tongue of God, the True, the Speaking, the Trustworthy King.

order.why: Read the contrast between verbal love of the Point and practical rejection.
shortened: Say: O people! Be not of those who name the Point of the Bayan as the Beloved while at the moment this name issueth from their mouths their eyes turn right and left in show of their longing for Him, yet they slay His very self and essence with the swords of rejection and turning away, and are not among those who perceive.

order.why: Examine the challenge to apply one’s own standard of righteousness.
shortened: Therefore, O people of the Bayan, be fair, for they said exactly what ye say today. Do ye enjoin righteousness upon men while forgetting for yourselves the melodies of God and then deny them?

order.why: Read the question comparing present conduct with conduct formerly condemned.
Keep the sharp accusation of repeating the earlier community’s arguments.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! If ye persist in your ways, why then did ye leave the community of the Furqan and enter into the party of God, the Almighty, the Most Exalted, the Most Great? For We observe you speaking as did the peoples of former times in those days, and advancing the same arguments as did the followers of religions past. It would behoove you, then, to return to your former path and follow your forbears of old.

order.why: Consider the warnings drawn from rejection of Muhammad and Jesus.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful and be not of those who disbelieved in Muhammad, the Messenger of God, when He came with the truth, and turned away from the Spirit when He appeared from the presence of a Mighty, Ancient One.

order.why: Read the account of earlier persecution as the source’s warning to its present audience.
Join that warning with an appeal for mercy toward oneself and others.
shortened: Say: Beware, O people of the Bayan! Have mercy upon yourselves and upon the souls of the servants, and be not like the people of the Furqan when the Most High came unto them with luminous Tablets of holiness.

order.why: Consider the harvest image for repeated patterns of action.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan, We behold you as We beheld them. Soon shall ye reap from the trees of your deeds the fruits which they reaped before. Take ye heed, O ye who are endued with insight!

order.why: Keep the severe comparative judgment as the source’s polemic.
Read the charge of heedlessness in its addressed setting.
shortened: Say: O concourse of the Bayan! By the True God, heedlessness and intoxication have seized you more severely than the peoples of old, and this is testified to by this truthful and trustworthy Pen.

order.why: Consider the claim that removed veils should help disclose others.
Read the accusation of dividing a universal Word.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Were ye to awaken even slightly and ascend somewhat toward the holy heaven of the Eternal Sovereign, ye would realize how ye have divided the blessed, universal, and eternal Word.

order.why: Keep the challenge to a spiritual claim paired with rejection.
Read the charge of idolatry in its polemical setting.
Consider the question about altered permissions and prohibitions.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Have ye forbidden what God hath made lawful unto you, or have ye made lawful what He hath forbidden, or have ye altered His decree from what was revealed in the Tablets of God, the Omnipotent, the Mighty, the Gracious?

order.why: Hear the complaint concerning treatment despite repeated announcement.
Keep the sweeping visionary testimony and accusation of a death sentence within the source.
Read the lament of the Points of Furqan and Bayan as scriptural imagery.
Consider the accusation of acts causing the heavenly company to lament.
shortened: O people of the Bayan! By God, ye have perpetrated that which hath caused the Primal Point and the Concourse on High and those settled in the Kingdom of Names to lament. Ye have committed that which none in the world hath committed, and perpetrated that which none among the peoples of the earth hath perpetrated.

order.why: Read the image of the Primal Point ashamed by his community’s words and actions.
Keep the urgent appeal for mercy amid suffering and threatened consequences.
shortened: His Beloved now waileth and weepeth, saying: "O people! Have mercy upon Him Who sat beneath the swords of the deniers, against Whom the followers of all religions have risen, conspiring at every moment to slay Him. If ye believed in the Exalted One (the Bab), why do ye wage war against His Beloved with the swords of rejection? If ye show no mercy to Him, then have mercy upon yourselves and be not of the wrongdoers."

order.why: Hear the concise appeal not to oppose the one who has come with verses.
Read the cry from the pit calling for fair judgment.
Consider a call to recognition spoken from imprisonment.
Read the contrast between resting at home and the exile described.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Do ye rest in your homes after the Ancient Beauty hath been exiled and settled in lands where none of its people, neither noble nor base, recognize Him?

order.why: Keep the forceful declaration of power beside questions about imprisonment and absence.
Consider the appeal not to dispute with one who has endured suffering.
Hear the Prisoner’s call to observe what the Tablets command.
Read the named contrast between martyrdom and denial as the source’s particular historical judgment.
Keep the warning concerning testing, mortality, and accumulated possessions.
shortened: Do ye imagine, O people of the Bayan and all who are on earth, that ye have believed in God and will not be tested thereafter? Nay, God will surely test you through His Cause that He may distinguish those who are upon truth from God's presence and are steadfast in God's religion. God shall soon annihilate your bodies and erase your traces and your names and all that ye have pursued and gathered unto yourselves and stored in your houses, and shall return you on the Day when the Sovereign of Eternity shall come with manifest dominion.

order.why: Read the selected warning about a lost opportunity with its source omission retained.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By the life of God, if anyone in this Revelation should miss a single matter, he shall never be able to make amends for it, now or ever....

order.why: Keep the severe command in its scriptural and polemical setting.
Consider the warning concerning fulfilled chastisement.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Whither do ye flee? The word of chastisement hath been fulfilled against him who hath denied the All-Merciful in this Revelation which hath shone forth from the horizon of all existence with manifest sovereignty.

order.why: Read the forceful prohibition of contention with the claimant in its own terms.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear God and contend not with Him with Whom should anyone contend, all who dwell in the highest Paradise and the realities of the Prophets and Messengers would curse him.

Read the appeal to righteousness in response to the stated proof.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Do ye dispute with Him Who hath come unto you with a proof wherewith all who are in the highest heavens could not prevail? Fear God and be of the righteous.

order.why: Consider the warning against placing others between oneself and the promised encounter.

Keep the warning concerning misleading speakers attributed to the source.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and follow not every sinful liar who hath barred you from the path of God and led you astray from this manifest announcement.

shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and follow not the dawning-places of idle fancies who have turned away from God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Consider evidence as the stated reason not to follow deniers.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful and follow not those who have denied the proof of God and His evidence after they were revealed in truth from this swift Pen.

order.why: Keep the smoke image of obstructed recognition.
Read the counsel concerning unnamed people and their words in its particular source setting.

Hear the brief warning against denial.
Read the source’s equation between opposition to the Cause and opposition to God.
Consider the direct appeal not to cast the offered truth behind oneself.

Say: "Fear ye God and cast not the Truth behind your backs. Take what ye have been given from the presence of One All-Knowing, All-Wise."

Keep the summons to read the Bayan and the warning concerning conduct.
Read the call to keep covenant and pledge.

order.why: Consider the stated insufficiency of inherited tales to restrain revelation.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! By God, the All-Merciful hath come with a sovereignty that your vain imaginings cannot withhold, nor what ye possess of the tales of old. Fear God and be not of the wrongdoers.

Fear God, O people, and follow not vain imaginings and idle fancies. Follow Him Who guideth you to His straight path and directeth you to the horizon of certitude.

shortened: Fear God, O people of the Bayan, and corrupt not the earth after its reformation, neither shed blood nor follow every sinful idolater.

order.why: Consider the injunction not to create religious discord.
shortened: Say: Beware, O people of the Bayan, lest ye create discord in the Cause and dispute in God's religion - this is better for you than that which ye do.

Consider the future community envisioned as free from corrupt desires.
shortened: The day is approaching when God will have, by an act of His Will, raised up a race of men the nature of which is inscrutable to all save God, the All-Powerful, the Self-Subsisting.  He shall purify them from the defilement of idle fancies and corrupt desires, shall lift them up to the heights of holiness, and shall cause them to manifest the signs of His sovereignty and might upon earth. Remember within yourselves what We have mentioned unto you in truth from this hidden and luminous Pen, and grieve not over anything, and turn not to the world and its ornaments and all that pertaineth to it and is in it and upon it, but turn to what is with God for that is better for you, if ye approach the shore of this counsel with the foot of detachment.
Be not veiled, O people of the Bayan, from this bounty which hath descended from the holy heaven while ye witness it with your own eyes.

order.why: Hear the concise appeal to trust rather than grief.
shortened: O people of the Bayan, grieve not over this, but put your trust in God - in Him let them that profess His unity place their trust.

order.why: Read the companion counsel of trust and following.
shortened: O people of the Bayan, be ye not disturbed by this, but place your trust in God, the Lord of all worlds.
O people of the Bayan, follow Me in all this, for this is better for you than all who are in the heavens and on earth.

order.why: Keep the brief reassurance addressed to the Bayan’s people.
shortened: O people of the Bayan! Grieve not at this, but put your trust in God, if ye be of them that know.

order.why: Read patience and recognition in the face of anticipated departure.
shortened: And ye, O people of the Bayan, hear My call at this moment and then know Me. Take heed of My counsel and beware lest ye transgress. When ye hear that the Servant hath migrated unto God, be ye not then disturbed nor grieve at anything, but be patient and be not of them who are impatient.

order.why: Hear the call to listen and trust.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Hearken unto My call, then put your trust in God, the Powerful, the Supreme, the Mighty.

Consider service joined with remembrance of sacrifice.
shortened: Arise to serve God and say: "O people of the Bayan! Your Lord, the All-Merciful, hath come with manifest sovereignty. Fear ye God and deny not Him for Whose path the blood of those near unto God was shed."

shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Are diverse lords better, or God, the One Powerful, Mighty, Peerless? Hold fast unto God and detach yourselves from all else - this is better for you, if you be of those who know.

Consider the appeal to mercy upon oneself and recognition of the promised One.

shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! Deny not Him Who has come with the truth from the presence of One mighty, powerful. He has come as 'Ali came from the heaven of the Cause with manifest sovereignty, and He commands you but what 'Ali commanded before. Fear God and be not of the deniers.
