subjects.displayTitle: Christ and Christianity: the Word, spiritual life, and the fruits of love
subjects.introduction: Walking past a dead animal with His disciples, Christ pointed to the whiteness of its teeth. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells that story because it shows the kind of sovereignty Christ exercised: not over territory, like Napoleon or Hannibal, but over hearts, a reign of love and mercy that prayed for its enemies from the cross. Bahá’u’lláh honours Christ as the Word of God, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains the title: a spotless mirror turned toward the sun, or a word that carries complete meaning where single letters carry none, so that the apostles become letters lit by the Word. The same teaching presses a hard question on anyone who bears Christ’s name. Peter denied Him three times and became the rock; Christian nations have waged war against the very peace He counselled. Love is the test of discipleship, and Jesus’ image of the vine whose branches must abide in Him to bear fruit [1] shows what that test means. The journey continues among the early disciples, into the crucifixion and resurrection, and toward the unity of religion.
subjects.arc: Begin with love and spiritual influence, explore the Word and its images, follow the transformation of disciples, examine suffering and historical reception, and return to the practical test of living the teachings.

order.why: Let the question about Christians and Bahais introduce the distinction between names and lived meaning.
shortened: Question: Are not all Christians Baha'is? Is there any difference?
Answer: When Christians act according to the teachings of Christ, they are called Baha'is. For the foundations of Christianity and the religion of Baha'u'llah are one.
Whoever acts completely in accordance with the teachings of Christ is a Baha'i. The purpose is the essential meaning of Christian, not the mere word.

order.why: Open with the story of Christ finding beauty where companions saw only decay.
shortened: It is said that Christ (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him) one day passed by a dead animal with the disciples. One said, "How putrid this animal is!" Another said, "What an ugly appearance it has!" Another said, "How repulsive it is!" Christ said, "Look at its teeth, how white they are!"

order.why: Consider sovereignty exercised in hearts rather than territory.
Read spiritual reign and the interpretation of restraining Satan.
shortened: O thou who art advancing toward God! Know verily that the reign of Jesus was a spiritual reign, penetrative in the hearts and the spirits and not ever the bodies, rocks and earth.
The fetters which Christ put on Satanis neck meant the breaking of his power, the hindering of his dominion and the dispersing of his assemblage through the power of Inspiration and Revelation.

order.why: Read the reported connection between love, mercy, and conduct toward enemies.
shortened: The principles of Christ's life were love and mercy. He prayed for his enemies on the cross. He came into the world in order to show men a new application of the Law of Love and he embodied this divine Idea in his life. He was the founder of the law of non-resistance.

order.why: Explore spiritual life and self-sacrifice as education and quickening.
shortened: The outward meaning is this:  Since Christ intended to promote a Cause that entailed the education of the human race, the quickening of the children of men, and the enlightenment of all humanity, and since promoting such a mighty Cause--a Cause that would antagonize all the peoples of the earth and withstand the opposition of every nation and government--was bound to bring about the spilling of His blood and to lead to His crucifixion and death, therefore at the moment He revealed His mission He offered up His life, welcomed the cross as His throne, regarded every wound as a balm and every poison as sweetest honey, and arose to instruct and guide the people.

order.why: Establish the stated Baha’i reverence for Christ as the Word of God.
Read the sun, mirror, letters, and Word explanation in full.
Hear the reported image of one heavenly song awakening many echoes.
Join divine oneness to fellowship among peoples.
shortened: He sent forth the Spirit (Christ) to summon all the world to His oneness, for acknowledgment of this oneness is the cause of fellowship and unity among the peoples of the world.

order.why: Consider all aspects of Christ’s life as testimony in the source’s account.
Read the stated magnitude of the revelation of Christ and Bahaullah.
shortened: Know that the attributes of perfection, the outpourings of divine grace, and the effulgences of divine revelation shine resplendent in all the Manifestations of God, but that the all-encompassing Word of God--Christ--and His Most Great Name--Baha'u'llah--have appeared with a revelation beyond all conception.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s concise identification of the Messiah as the Word.
Read the Bab’s statement of Christ as Messenger within its own language.
Consider the summons to guidance through divine light.
Read the extended reported theological dialogue, its questions, and its interpretive approach.
shortened: Rather, what is meant by the Word is that the world of creation is like letters, and all humans are like letters. A letter alone has no meaning, no independent meaning, but Christ's station is that of the Word, which has complete and independent meaning. Therefore He is called the Word. What is meant by complete meaning is the emanations of divine perfections, for the perfections of other souls are partial, not their own, and derived from others. But the reality of Christ possessed complete and independent perfections.

'For example, this lamp is illumined, the moon is illumined, but their light is not of themselves - it is derived from another. But Christ was like the sun - His light was His own, not borrowed from another. Therefore we interpret Him as the Word, meaning a comprehensive reality possessing complete perfections.

order.why: Revisit the distinction between isolated letters and meaningful words.
Read the reported definition of the Word through virtues and bestowals.
Keep the reported comparison of the titles Son and Word attributed to its conversation.
Explore how letters receive significance and grace from the Word.
shortened: It is evident that the Letter is a member of the Word, and this membership in the Word signifieth that the Letter is dependent for its value on the Word, that is, it deriveth its grace from the Word; it has a spiritual kinship with the Word, and is accounted an integral part of the Word. The Apostles were even as Letters, and Christ was the essence of the Word Itself; and the meaning of the Word, which is grace everlasting, cast a splendor on those Letters.

order.why: Consider the unity of sunlight reflected in distinct mirrors.
shortened: The Christ reality was like unto a pure mirror and the Sun of Reality shone upon it from the Holy Horizon. Therefore, it became evident that the sun is one with regard to reality but manifesting itself in all mirrors.

order.why: Read the contrast between Christ and others through the source’s paired images.
Preserve the companion statement separately with its own identity.
shortened: The difference between Christ and others is this:  Christ was the Spirit, others are bodies.  Christ was the Sun, others are mirrors.  Christ was the Truth and was bestowing Eternal Life; others are dead and are imparting deadness and negligence.

order.why: Distinguish pre-existence in essence and distinction from earthly honor.
Read greatness as divine perfections rather than a circumstance of birth.
shortened: It follows clearly from this verse of John that even the existence of the Apostles proceeds from a spiritual reality rather than from a material power. The honour and greatness of Christ reside not in His being without a father, but rather in His divine perfections, outpourings, and splendours. Were the greatness of Christ due to His lacking a father, Adam would be even greater, for He had neither father nor mother.

order.why: Keep the answer concerning spiritual and bodily perfection in its own terms.
Read the reported discussion of family and sonship without merging it with other accounts.
Consider the Gospel saying concerning goodness and God.
shortened: Even when someone addressed Christ and called Him good, He responded, "Why callest thou me good? For there is none good but One, that is God."

order.why: Read the brief reported distinction between a passing word and enduring meaning.
Keep the reported philosophical account of letters, numbers, and appearances in its own setting.
Explore fire, spirit, and the reflection of meaning in words.
Read the poem’s tears, humility, and love as a different mode of approach.
Consider spiritual nourishment through the image of living bread.
Read heavenly food as the spiritual teaching flowing from Christ.
Keep the interpretation of the Eucharist as the source’s theological argument.
Read baptism through repentance, example, and the customs of its time.
shortened: As Christ desired that this custom instituted by John be practiced by all at that time, He Himself submitted to it, that souls might be awakened and that the law which had issued from the former religion might be fulfilled. For even though this custom was instituted by John, it represented in reality the purification of repentance which has been practiced in all the divine religions.
It is not that Christ was in need of baptism, but He submitted to it because at that time this action was praiseworthy and acceptable before God and presaged the glad tidings of the Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the reported saying about grapes and the Kingdom with its source context.
Read the distinct report of the fruit of the vine without blending accounts.
Consider the simple room of the Last Supper.
Read the reported image of renewed fellowship in every world.
Explore the lasting effects of a small spiritual assembly.
shortened: Although this assembly is now limited to a few souls, yet since it is a divine assembly, like the assembly of the Lord's Supper of Christ, it will expand day by day until it spreads throughout all regions. Consider how the small assembly of the Lord's Supper of Christ, when confirmed by the Holy Spirit, produced such mighty results and great effects!

order.why: Consider the seed image and continuing fruit.
Read the call of the fisherman into a new form of service.
Keep the reported question about humble disciples and their influence.
shortened: Jesus Christ did not come from the world of princes or scientists. Outwardly he was but an humble artisan, his disciples simple fishermen. Why were these disciples able to do what philosophers and scientists failed to accomplish?

order.why: Read the interpretation of speaking in tongues, retaining its historical assertions as source claims.
shortened: Therefore, the Holy Spirit endowed the Apostles with the tongue of the Kingdom, and they spoke with all peoples as if in their own tongue; that is, whenever they conversed with a person of any faith or nation, it was as though they were speaking his own tongue. Were it otherwise, there are at present more than a thousand known languages and it would be fair to expect that the Apostles would have written at least one Gospel in the language of one of the other nations. It is, however, well established that the Gospel was written only in Hebrew and in Greek.

order.why: Consider the reported interpretation of Peter’s confession and the rock.
Read the companion account of Peter’s role in resolving differences.
shortened: Notwithstanding that his holiness Christ said nothing about Peter except the one word, 'Thou art the rock and upon this rock I build my church,' this word became cause of dispelling differences, so that whatever Peter said the others would accept.

order.why: Preserve the differing reported emphasis on the absence of an appointed center.
shortened: There were dissensions after the departure of Christ because there had been no Center appointed. Did Christ say to anyone, "You are the Centre of my Covenant, you are the explainer of my book?"

order.why: Read the account of Arius and covenant within its historical argument.
shortened: Sometime after Christ, Arius, the Patriarch of Alexandria, founded a new sect. He was an orator, articulate of speech and a very audacious and powerful person who succeeded in bringing one and a half million people under his influence. He even secured the allegiance of the Emperor Constantine. But since he deviated from the Covenant of Christ, at the end he faded away and perished. This Covenant was based on the words addressed to Peter, "Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." And though these words attributed to Christ are based only on the report of some of His disciples, nevertheless Christian unity was preserved for eight hundred years through this implicit Covenant.

order.why: Keep the companion account of Arius distinct and attributed.
shortened: Consider thou, at the time of Christ and after Him, how many childish attempts have been made by different persons!  What claims they have advanced and what a multitude have they gathered around themselves!  Even Arius attracted to himself a million and a half followers and strove and endeavoured to sow the seeds of sedition in the Cause of Christ.

order.why: Consider the brief reported observation concerning subsequent sects.
shortened: You see how many sects and religions appeared after Christ. Now the Blessed Beauty has designated one point so that no differences would remain.

order.why: Read the accounts of testing, denial, and betrayal as a challenge to steadfastness.
shortened: Christ said, "Fast, so that you may not fall into temptation." Verily, tests withheld a great Apostle (Judas) from the Mercy of God, and made him take part in the shedding of the blood of Christ.  The tests made Peter the Apostle deny Christ.  The tests made the Brethren of Christ deny Him; many a just, faithful and assured souls did not endure the power of the tests but turned backward, until he reached the lowest of the low.

order.why: Explore the contrast between shaken followers and enduring disciples.
Keep the reported description of consternation after the crucifixion.
shortened: After the crucifixion of Christ the few apostles who were left behind were thrown into a state of utter consternation and agitation. Peter who was the chief of Apostles denied the Lord thrice...

order.why: Read the reported growth into understanding and fidelity.
shortened: Even as in the time of Jesus the Son of Mary, those who were under the shadow of Christ knew not in what shadow they dwelt, but afterwards they proved faithful. May my soul be a sacrifice for them! Yet during His own time they achieved nothing.

order.why: Consider the source’s comparison of circumstances, followers, and certitude.
shortened: At the time of His ascension, Christ had raised up twelve men and four women. There were to be sure a few others beside these, but they had not reached the station of certitude. And among these twelve men, one became His sworn enemy: Judas Iscariot, who, notwithstanding his position as the chief of the Apostles, arose to have Him killed. The most prominent among the remaining eleven was Peter, and even he failed to stand firm in the face of trials, since, according to the explicit text of the Gospel, he thrice denied Christ at the hour of His martyrdom, to the point of entirely recanting his faith in the last instance. It was only after the cock crowed that he was reawakened and made contrite and repentant.

order.why: Keep the companion comparison’s numerical and historical claims attributed.
shortened: When Christ ascended, only a small number had become believers and were assured, and the greatest of the apostles was Peter the renowned. Despite this, he denied Christ three times. But observe the Cause of the Blessed Beauty - at the time of His ascension, hundreds of thousands of souls were gathered under the banner of certainty and were in complete steadfastness and firmness. The proof of this is that hundreds upon hundreds hastened to the field of martyrdom with utmost joy and gladness and sacrificed their lives and property.

order.why: Preserve the brief count of believers without harmonizing differing accounts.
shortened: At the time of Christ's ascension there were eleven believers. Now see what is happening! Praise be to God, the call is raised in Africa, and in Asia the Turk and Tajik are awakened, and from America the shot of the unity of mankind reaches the ear of every poor and noble one.

order.why: Read the reported comparison of steadfastness in its addressed setting.
shortened: The people are exceedingly heedless. They must be made to understand by force how agitated people became in the time of Christ - even Peter denied Him three times. But in this Most Great Cause, the companions and loved ones remained so firm and steadfast that they gave up their lives dancing and stamping their feet in the field of sacrifice, and their firmness, steadfastness and self-sacrifice astonished minds.

order.why: Keep the extended pilgrim account of teachings, scope, and followers clearly attributed.
shortened: If you gather together all the teachings of Christ they will not exceed ten pages. If you gather together the teachings of the BLESSED PERFECTION they will exceed sixty or seventy volumes. Those of Christ have no new laws, except the regulation about divorce. Those of the BLESSED PERFECTION contain many instructions. The greatest teachings of Jesus Christ are such as these: Love you enemies; bless those who curse you and revile you; when struck on the right cheek turn the left. Of course, these commands are right, and what is contained in the world can not equal them in value; but these instructions refer particularly to individuals, and do not deal with nations. They are personal, not universal. Those of the BLESSED PERFECTION are for all nations, like the injunction for universal peace, although even these apply to individuals as well as to nations.

order.why: Read the reported relation of the duration of a mission to its circumstances.
Consider the reported vision of worldwide peace and fellowship.
Read the reported bud and flower image for continuity and expansion.
Consider seasons and medicine as images of renewed revelation.
shortened: There are seasons in the revelation from God, as in the natural year, and just as the Christ manifested the Spirit of God in the flesh and helped the earth in his time, now the message of Baha'Ullah is the medicine of which the world has much need.

order.why: Keep the reported call to act on both the Gospel and Bahaullah’s teachings.
Read the concise statement about renewed meaning in ancient law.
Consider the reported purpose of promoting the Torah.
Read the source’s account of Christ extending the recognition of Moses.
Keep the reported account of moral education and reverence for Moses.
shortened: Christ -- this single and unique Personage -- appeared amongst these despised and degraded people, reflecting a divine power and the potency of the Holy Spirit. He unified the various peoples and nations of the world, brought them together in fellowship and agreement and gathered them beneath the overshadowing protection of one Word.

All Christians believe in Moses. They declare that He was a Man of God, the Interlocutor and Prophet of God, that His Book was the Book of God, that the people of Israel were the people of God and that all the prophets of Israel were valid and true. They offer unlimited praise, sincere eulogy, and manifest unlimited love for the religion of Moses.

order.why: Read the reported account of Christ’s influence in relation to Israel and other peoples.
Consider the source’s proposed test of prophethood through education.
Read the universal and altruistic character ascribed to Christ’s teaching.
Explore transformation of moral life in the reported address.
shortened: For example, Christ educated and developed mankind universally. He rescued nations and peoples from the bondage of superstition and idolatry. He summoned them all to the knowledge of the oneness of God. They were dark, they became illumined; they were material, they became spiritual; earthly they were, they became heavenly. He enlightened the world of morality.

order.why: Consider the reported invitation to examine perfections and teachings directly.
Read the source’s argument about divine education overcoming enmity.
shortened: It is therefore evident that mankind requires a universal divine educator who can gather the diverse peoples under the shadow of one Word, cause contending nations to drink from a single fountain, transform enmity and hatred into love and fellowship, and convert strife and conflict into peace and tranquility.

Likewise, Christ (peace be upon Him) gathered together the antagonistic, hostile, and warring peoples of Greece, Rome, Syria, Chaldea, and Assyria who were filled with the utmost hatred and enmity, uniting them at one fountain and establishing complete harmony among them.

order.why: Keep the reported historical picture of formerly hostile peoples united.
shortened: Again, consider Christ: how that marvelous expression of unity bestowed education and ethical training upon the Roman, Greek, Egyptian, Syrian and Assyrian nations and welded together a people from them in a permanent and indissoluble bond. These nations were formerly at enmity and in a state of continual hostility and strife. He cemented them together, caused them to agree, conferred tranquillity upon humanity and established the foundations of human welfare throughout the world.

order.why: Read the reported relation between unity and cultural inheritance.
shortened: Christ appeared in this world nineteen hundred years ago to establish ties of unity and bonds of love between the various nations and different communities. He cemented together the sciences of Rome and the splendors of the civilization of Greece.

order.why: Consider the address’s account of renewed life and influence.
shortened: As to Christ the Glorious, the Word of God and the Spirit of God, who upheld the Gospel, God raised him up among a subject people who had accepted bondage and silenced their own voices before the power of Rome. He breathed the spirit of life into them, and revived them after their death, and made them the foremost in the land. The Romans were humbled before them, Greece submitted to them, and their reputation spread around the world, to the present day.

order.why: Read the reported transition from ignorance to knowledge through the sun image.
Keep the brief reported claim concerning education of Western nations.
Read unity as the source’s evidence for Christ’s station.
Consider spiritual influence spreading without outward support.
Read the movement from East to West as an unfolding of capacities.
Keep the reported contrast between outward means and transformative influence.
Read the reported contrast between levels of human response and spiritual education.
shortened: Yes, this is true, but one man is so exalted that others bow down before Him and He is adored by them like Christ or Moses, who called people to the oneness of divinity and who became the cause of the education of a nation, while another is so degraded that he bows down before dust and worships ants and serpents.
But observe what a banner of unique being Christ unfurled without friend or helper.

order.why: Consider outward poverty beside sovereignty of hearts.
Read the crown of poverty and heavenly treasure together.
Keep the reported connection with the blessing on the poor.
Read the reported humble origins of Christ and the disciples.
Consider the call to follow Christ’s example amid hardship.
shortened: His Holiness Christ delivered the Cause of God in the wilderness of the Holy Land, with bare feet, old clothing, thirsty and hungry.
Be thou follow (the example of) His Holiness Christ until thou mayst succeed.

order.why: Read the prayer of gratitude amid material deprivation.
Keep the extended reported storm and thanksgiving narrative in its own setting.
Read the reported remembrance of teaching beside the Sea of Galilee.
Consider the reported spiritual associations of Carmel, Haifa, and Nazareth.
shortened: His Holiness Christ always used to cross this Mount Carmel, Haifa and Nazareth. Therefore these cities and this mountain have a spiritual atmosphere.

order.why: Keep the brief reported observation about later attention to Christ’s visits.
shortened: Christ, in His own land, entered Jerusalem and the assemblies of the Israelites several times and gave counsels and exhortations. Consider how much importance Christian clergy later gave to this matter.

order.why: Read the invitation to reflect on Christ, Mary, and subsequent events.
shortened: Reflect upon the matter of the ascetic of the world, namely Christ, and His mother, and likewise upon the events that transpired after the ascension of the Spirit.

order.why: Explore the account of rejection and the interpretation of signs of return.
shortened: These are the melodies, sung by Jesus, Son of Mary, in accents of majestic power in the Ridvan of the Gospel, revealing those signs that must needs herald the advent of the Manifestation after Him. In the first Gospel according to Matthew it is recorded: And when they asked Jesus concerning the signs of His coming, He said unto them: "Immediately after the oppression of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the earth shall be shaken: and then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

order.why: Read the source’s account of expectations that obstructed recognition.
Keep the reported seed, flower, and fruit image of Moses and Christ.
shortened: Regarding the appearance of Christ, there were many prophecies in the bible which foretold his coming... The teachings of Moses were like a seed, but when the seed grew into a plant and bore blossom, then fruit--the fruit signified Christ, who was the result of all the teachings of Moses...

order.why: Explains universal love through Christ’s love for His persecutors.
Consider the warning that confidence in civilization can conceal a spiritual need.
Read the reported warning against letting outward appearance veil spiritual reality.
shortened: May the world be for you no obstacle hiding the Sun of Truth from your sight, as the human body of Christ hid his divinity from the people of his day.

order.why: Read the Gospel citations concerning the Kingdom and coming into light.
shortened: In one place He says: "And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth." And in another place it is mentioned: "Light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God."

order.why: Keep the reported appeal concerning seeing, hearing, understanding, and healing.
Read the account of ridicule and suffering as the source presents it.
Keep the brief remembrance of poverty and persecution attributed.
Read the reported challenge to an idealized image of immediate acceptance.
shortened: The Christians now think that when Christ declared Himself that all the people ran and kissed his Hands and Feet. On the contrary, He had always to hide Himself, while the Blessed Perfection never hid Himself.

order.why: Keep the account of hostile claims as reported accusations, not endorsed history.
Read the source’s pointed question about guilt and crucifixion in its own setting.
Consider sacrifice for release from discord and enmity.
Keep the reported elixir image and account of influence after death attributed.
Read the reported survival of a cause against powerful resistance.
Keep the reported persecution narrative and its historical claims in source context.
Read the distinct reported account of opposition giving way to investigation.
shortened: Christianity in France was emancipated in this manner. One of the monarchs in France realized that no matter how many Christians were slain, it bore no fruit. One day he summoned his ministers and consulted [with them]. Thereupon, he announced that he bore no opposition whatsoever to Christianity. This resulted in all the people being enticed to investigate, and gradually they became Christian.
In this Cause, it will also occur likewise.

order.why: Preserve the reported historical comparison and expectation without turning it into an editorial forecast.
shortened: It took three hundred years for the Cause of Christ to be spread but in the first century the Cause of Baha'u'llah will be promoted everywhere.

order.why: Keep the reported history of the Sepulchre attributed to the account.
shortened: The Holy Sepulchre of Christ was a place for dumping all kinds of rubbish for three hundred years till St Helena came, cleared the ground and built over it a most wonderful church.

order.why: Read the source’s distinction between views of Christ after crucifixion.
Consider heaven as a term requiring interpretation.
Read the reported affirmation of Christ’s enduring presence.
Keep the commentary on John and its disagreement with another interpretation clearly attributed.
shortened: This is but one melody from the melodies of the Gospel that was revealed concerning the Pride of the Messengers. However, as the Christian people have fallen into the wilderness of error and blindness, they have disregarded this explicit statement without any ambiguity, and have clung to vain interpretations, saying that what was meant by these verses was the Holy Spirit that descended upon the disciples after Christ's ascension.
This is the custom of all peoples, that they close their eyes to the clear meanings of the divine verses and cling to vain interpretations of ambiguous passages.

order.why: Read the direct question concerning the One to whom Christ ascended.
Consider the reported use of the prayer for the coming Kingdom.
shortened: The Master replied:
"It is nearly two thousand years since His holiness the Lord Christ taught this prayer to His people: "Thy Kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth, as it is in Heaven.'

order.why: Read the reported comparison with the Quranic clay-bird account.
Keep the companion report concerning speech in the cradle.
Consider the invitation to investigate reverence for Christ in the Quran.
Read the report of defending Christ and Muhammad in a synagogue.
Keep the reported account of Bahaullah’s praise of Christ.
shortened: Christ was the Word of God, the Spirit of God. The Blessed Beauty made His station manifest in the East. The people of the East did not read the Torah and the Gospel; Baha'u'llah spread them in the East. He mentioned Christ with utmost sanctity; He did not mention anyone else like Christ.

order.why: Read the companion affirmation of Christ’s exalted station.
Consider the source’s experience of rejection while defending Christ.
Keep the reported comparison of titles and spirituality attributed.
Read the reported conversation moving from Christ’s station to sectarian division.
Keep the critique of religious decline within the historical argument of the source.
Read the reported criticism of religious and political power without generalizing it editorially.
Keep the reported contrast between early suffering and later self-interest.
Read the reported warning concerning imitation in its conversational setting.
Consider the reported challenge concerning bells and the divine call.
shortened: For nineteen hundred years they have rung the church bell, yet they have grown neither weary nor tired. They regard the sound of copper and brass as the divine call, though it be but inanimate matter, and they hold it sacred and answer its summons, rushing forthwith to church.

order.why: Keep the reported critique of inherited sin and missionary education as a particular argument.
shortened: It is equally false when the Christian missionaries place the whole emphasis on original sin, consider man as impure and corrupted from the time in the mother's womb, and when they, as the 'instrument of the Almighty', expect all salvation from their schooling and training of the small sinner.

order.why: Read the reported challenge about unity, hierarchy, and slavery.
shortened: The Christian Church with its hierarchy of clerics has reversed Christ's and Paul's teaching of unity. His Holiness Christ has set the slave beside the master, and what has the Church of the 19th century said to the slavery of the Negroes of America?

order.why: Consider the distinction the report draws between seclusion and practical service.
Read the reported priority given to Christ’s own words.
Keep the reported invitation to examine the New Testament directly.
Read the reported preference for the Sermon on the Mount.
Consider the contrast between Christ’s restraint and religiously justified violence.
shortened: Christ forbade war! When the disciple Peter, thinking to defend his Lord, cut off the ear of the servant of the High Priest, Christ said to him: 'Put up thy sword into the sheath'. Yet, in spite of the direct command of the Lord they profess to serve -- men still dispute, make war, and kill one another, and His counsels and teaching seem quite forgotten.

order.why: Keep the reported question concerning swords with its available source context.
Read the reported return to the sheathed sword and the other cheek.
Consider love for enemies as a test of professed discipleship.
Read the reported question about war’s consequences for families.
Keep the reported critique of European armament in its 1914 context.
Read the extended wartime argument that conduct can oppose the teacher one claims to follow.
shortened: These Christian nations wage war against Christ. Any Christian who opposeth the teachings of Christ hath risen in opposition to Him. These swords strike at Christ. These bullets are aimed at Christ.

Strange it is that they call themselves Christians, utter the name of Christ, read the Gospel, yet Christ is clear of them. Were Christ to descend from heaven and were they to say "These are Thy people," He would say: "God forbid! These are Thy people in word only, but in truth they are the people of Caiaphas."

order.why: Consider the contrast between coercion over bodies and love in hearts.
shortened: Jesus Christ established the religion of God through love. His sovereignty is everlasting. Napoleon overthrew governments in war and bloodshed. His dominion passed away; he himself was dethroned. Bonaparte destroyed human life; Christ was a Savior. Bonaparte controlled the physical bodies of men; Christ was a conqueror of human hearts.

order.why: Read the reported interpretation of the Lamb’s defense as teachings.
Consider the warning contained in the image of a fruitless tree.
shortened: And Christ says that the owner of an orchard will not leave a withered tree in the garden but will surely cut it down and cast it into the fire, for dried wood is fit and worthy only for the fire.

order.why: Read the reported tree image as a question about the results of religious life.
Keep the reported demand that spiritual life produce visible effects.
shortened: We cannot believe the call to be spiritual when there is no result. Spirit is reality, and when the spirit in each of us seeks to join itself with the Great Reality, it must in turn give life. The Jews in the time of Christ were dead, having no real life, and Jesus actually wafted a new breath into their bodies. Behold what has been accomplished since!

order.why: Return to the call to remember principles taught through word and deed.
shortened: For many years Christ taught these eternal principles in this holy land through both word and deed. He journeyed throughout Palestine, and gradually His teachings spread throughout the world. But alas, a hundred thousand times alas, that people have forgotten those divine principles.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the companion reported story of the dead animal.
shortened: They say that one day His Holiness Christ – may My spirit by a sacrifice unto Him – and His Apostle passed by a dog that had died and was decaying.

order.why: Read the supplied Gospel line with its own citation and retained match status.
Keep the supplied fragment about letters and words visibly incomplete.
Read the supplied passage connecting distinct prophetic encounters.
Consider the supplied distinction between unconscious obedience and discerning faith.
shortened: Know that faith is of two kinds. The first is objective faith that is expressed by the outer man, obedience of the limbs and senses. The other faith is subjective, and unconscious obedience to the will of God.

This condition of unconscious obedience constitutes subjective faith. But the discerning faith that consists of true knowledge of God and the comprehension of divine words, of such faith there is very little in any age. That is why His Holiness Christ said to His followers, "Many are called but few are chosen."

order.why: Close with the supplied account of love, courage, and the good of humanity.
